reports.method: Real generated JS factories and WASM through unchanged Ymf276/OpnVariant and actual YMF276Synth/OPNDirectTransport. Exact Float32 stereo PCM, all bus reads/status/IRQ after each fixture event (register-pair events or individual bus-byte events) and render chunk, partition invariance, selected reset/reprogram replay and post-scenario continuation probes. Independent YMF276 mixed-output DAC formula over all 256 codes, ninth-bit and pan combinations, warm DAC/address/reset, mismatched-bus, timer, six-channel stereo and owned-buffer controls. No tolerance or mock.
limits: sampleRate(clock) calculates floor(clock/144); it does not set a chip clock or output rate. The listed pitch clocks only quantize authored frequency registers. No dynamic clock/rate configuration or resampler is claimed.

The actual 11-function C ABI and OpnVariant have no save/load/state facade, native mute, borrowed-view/Into generation or low-level observers. Synth getState is a JS register model, not a restorable native snapshot.

Status/read/IRQ observations are after every fixture bus event and rendered chunk plus a continuation probe, not a per-master-clock hardware trace. Synth callbacks are exercised only on the real supported Synth consumer.

Reset clears FM registers/operator phase and adapter timers/IRQ; the native core retains DAC data/enable/address and some engine counters. Warm reset/reprogram is compared across builds, not claimed identical to a fresh instance.

YMF276 mixed 14-bit FM output and DAC output-shift scaling and existing timer/reset/port behavior are current core/adapter controls for build parity, not a physical hardware accuracy claim. No YMF276 VGM AudioEngine or player route is invented.

Only synchronous Node/WASM and the actual direct Synth consumer are exercised. Browser, Worklet scheduling, general Mixer/Playground, Native/Tauri, physical output and listening judgments are outside scope.
reports.frameCountScope: Both builds: scenario bodies and 127-frame continuation probes, selected reset/reprogram replays, bounded wrapper controls and real Synth output. A stereo frame is one left/right pair; no source or delivered frames are double-counted.
